Sarah / Nova ops team —

Thanks again for the time today. To get our dedicated capacity proposal into a draft we need a couple of concrete numbers from your side so we can map to H100 / A100 / L4 tradeoffs and give a realistic reserve/burst plan: 

1) Expected 95th-percentile qps for token-generation (requests/sec) across your two primary models (Summarizer and Clinical-Reranker). If you can provide both avg tokens-per-request and target p95 latency SLOs that helps.
2) Typical context window for the Summarizer (avg and tail). You mentioned occasionally hitting 32k tokens — can you confirm how often (>1% of requests?).
3) Concurrency target for the Dedicated pool (simultaneous sessions). Is the plan to run all prod traffic on Dedicated or to split host/burst?

If easier, drop the workload spreadsheet you used internally; I can baseline throughput and memory working set and produce a slotting plan (reserved H100/A100 vs L4 burst) plus an ops playbook for fallthroughs and eviction.

I attached a small template (nova_workload_profile.xlsx) — fill or dump a sample and I’ll iterate.

cheers,
Mateo

Kimberly / Dev —

Sarah sent the workload sheet and a useful note about regulatory constraints on truncation (attached). High level numbers: p95 token rates 120 t/s for summarizer, 30 t/s for reranker, 220 concurrent sessions target on Dedicated to cover ~60% steady-state. Tail contexts occasionally hit 32k (1.5%).

I’m drafting a recommendation but want quick takes on two points:
A) Memory binning for Summarizer: for sessions with >=16k context we should prefer A100 80GB instances to avoid repeated KV cache eviction due to memory churn. H100 can offer higher throughput but A100 80GB reduces fragmentation and tiling for long-context KV.
B) For concurrency-first path (shorter contexts, high qps) H100 gives better tokens/sec per GPU and lower tokens-per-dollar; L4 is attractive as a cost-efficient burst tier for lower-latency short-context inference (and safe fallthrough when Dedicated is saturated).

I'd like a quick ops-playbook sketch: reserved mix (A100 80GB slots for long-context heavy sessions), H100 reserved for throughput-first slots, and an L4 burst pool with automatic routing. Also propose a 10% reserved headroom buffer and an eviction policy (prefer L4 fallback before truncation, but honor the regulatory note).

Can you both weigh in with constraints (kernel availability, quantized performance expectations, slotting algorithm compatibility) — I’ll make a client-facing MAP afterward.

-Mateo

Quick technical notes from infra / runtime side: 

- Kernel support: both H100 and A100 have full optimized attention kernels in our runtime. H100 wins on FP8 paths and larger batch throughput; A100 80GB avoids out-of-core problems for 32k windows without aggressive tiling. L4 is well-supported but we only expose a limited KV cache (smaller per-slot) — good for short-context sessions but will incur re-computation for long-history sessions.

- Quantization: For Summarizer we can run q8_0 on H100 for best throughput; A100 shows smaller degradation in 8-bit heaps for long contexts due to memory layout. Recommend running Summarizer q8 on H100 for short/median contexts, A100 80GB q4/q5 for >16k contexts.

- Slotting heuristic: propose simple affinity policy: tag incoming request by estimated context_size and latency SLO. Affinity rules: context >= 16k -> slot to A100 pool; context <16k & latency SLO <= 250ms -> H100; all other -> L4 burst. Reserve headroom: 10% for each pool + 5% global safety.

- Eviction/fallthrough: fallback order: L4 burst (if within regulatory boundaries) -> Hosted API -> degrade sampling / increase temperature? (joke) — practically we route to Hosted with rate-limit gating and notify ops.

Dev, any numbers on expected tokens/sec per GPU (empirics) for these exact models? I can include microbenchmarks in the MAP.

-kim

Sharing quick empirical numbers from the perf lab for the two models (single-GPU, steady-state primed KV cache):

- model-sum-v2 (1.2k avg tokens/request): H100 (fp8/q8) ~ 36k tokens/sec; A100 80GB (q4/q5) ~ 18k tokens/sec; L4 (int8) ~ 4.5k tokens/sec. For long contexts (>16k) effective throughput drops ~25% on H100 due to KV churn; A100 maintains within 5-10% of baseline.
- ranker-v3 (350 avg tokens): H100 ~ 9k t/s; A100 ~ 4.5k t/s; L4 ~ 1.6k t/s.

Slot sizing draft (to meet p95 SLOs with 10% headroom): 
- Summarizer steady portion (60% of total traffic mapped to Dedicated): need equivalent of ~6 H100 GPUs or ~12 A100 80GB GPUs if we only used one SKU.
- Reranker steady portion: ~2 H100 or ~4 A100.

Hybrid reserved plan (recommended): 
- Reserved: 4 H100 + 6 A100(80GB) — H100 handles short/high-qps sessions; A100 reserved for long-context sessions.
- Burst pool: 24 L4 slots (autoscaling) to pick up spikes; route short-context spikes here first.
- Headroom: keep 10% additional reserved computed as float and enforce via autoscaler.

I've also attached a quick PDF with the math and slot equivalence table (proposed-sku-split.pdf).

-dev

Subject: Final MAP draft + ops playbook (NovaHealth)

Sarah —

Appended is our draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP-NovaHealth-v1.docx) and the proposed SKU split (proposed-sku-split.pdf). Key decisions summarized: 

1) Reserved mix: 4 x H100 + 6 x A100 (80GB) to cover Dedicated steady-state (60% traffic). This combination meets p95 SLOs while limiting memory churn for long-context Summarizer runs.
2) Burst pool: autoscaled L4 (initial target 24 slots) for short-context spikes; routing policy sends short, latency-sensitive requests to H100 first, then L4; long-context affinity strictly prefers A100 pool.
3) Headroom and safety: 10% reserved headroom per pool + 5% global safety reserve. We will provision incremental slots in month-1 if 95th-percentile utilization > 75% for any pool.
4) Eviction/fallthrough policy: If Dedicated pools saturate: a) route eligible short-context requests to L4 burst; b) route regulatory-sensitive long-context requests to Hosted with explicit throttling only with prior consent from Nova ops; c) as last resort apply model-level truncation (documented and only after ops approval).
5) Quantization profile: Summarizer -> H100 (q8) for <=16k; A100 (q4/q5) for >16k. Ranker -> H100 q8 preferred.

Next steps: sign-off on MAP and we’ll schedule a 60-minute ops handoff to go through the runbooks, alerting thresholds, and the automated failover tests. I put a tentative HubSpot task (DEAL-5492) and Drive folder link in the MAP.

If this looks good I’ll send the formal quote (reserve schedule + burst billing assumptions) and an ops runbook with playbook checks (autoscaler thresholds, alerting, and canary step-down flow).

Thanks and happy holidays —
Mateo
